cues.en: and when they finally come face-to-face with the statue,

cues.en: they both freeze dead in their tracks.

cues.zh: 第一个人——我们叫他Adam——
cues.en: The first guy -- we'll call him Adam --

cues.zh: 被完美人体形态的美震撼住了。
cues.en: is transfixed by the beauty of the perfect human form.

cues.en: The second guy -- we'll call him Bill --

cues.en: is transfixed by embarrassment, at staring at the thing there in the center.

cues.zh: 那么我的问题是：
cues.en: So here's my question for you:

cues.en: Which one of these two guys was more likely to have voted for George Bush,

cues.en: which for Al Gore?

cues.en: I don't need a show of hands,

cues.en: because we all have the same political stereotypes.

cues.zh: 我们都知道是Bill。
cues.en: We all know that it's Bill.

cues.en: And in this case, the stereotype corresponds to reality.

cues.zh: 自由派在一个叫“经验开放性”的重要人格特质上确实远高于保守派，
cues.en: It really is a fact that liberals are much higher than conservatives

cues.zh: 这是事实。
cues.en: on a major personality trait called openness to experience.

cues.zh: 开放性高的人
cues.en: People who are high in openness to experience

cues.zh: 就是渴望新奇、多样、差异、新想法、旅行。
cues.en: just crave novelty, variety, diversity, new ideas, travel.

cues.zh: 开放性低的人喜欢熟悉的东西，
cues.en: People low on it like things that are familiar,

cues.zh: 安全可靠的东西。
cues.en: that are safe and dependable.

cues.zh: 如果你了解这个特质，
cues.en: If you know about this trait,

cues.zh: 你就能理解很多关于人类行为的谜题，
cues.en: you can understand a lot of puzzles about human behavior,

cues.zh: 比如为什么艺术家和会计师如此不同。

cues.en: You can predict what kinds of books they like to read,

cues.en: and what kinds of food they like to eat.

cues.en: Once you understand this trait,

cues.zh: 你就能理解为什么会有人在Applebee's吃饭，
cues.en: you can understand why anybody would eat at Applebee's,

cues.zh: 但不是你认识的任何人。
cues.en: but not anybody that you know.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: This trait also tells us a lot about politics.

cues.en: The main researcher of this trait, Robert McCrae,

cues.en: says that "Open individuals have an affinity

cues.en: for liberal, progressive, left-wing political views ..."

cues.en: They like a society which is open and changing,

cues.zh: 而封闭的人更偏好
cues.en: "... whereas closed individuals prefer

cues.en: conservative, traditional, right-wing views."

cues.zh: 这个特质也告诉我们很多关于人们会加入什么群体。
cues.en: This trait also tells us a lot about the kinds of groups people join.

cues.en: Here's the description of a group I found on the web.

cues.en: What kinds of people would join

cues.en: "a global community ... welcoming people from every discipline and culture,

cues.en: and who hope to turn that understanding into a better future for us all"?

cues.en: This is from some guy named Ted.

cues.en: Well, let's see now.

cues.en: If openness predicts who becomes liberal,

cues.en: and openness predicts who becomes a TEDster,

cues.en: then might we predict that most TEDsters are liberal?

cues.en: Let's find out.

cues.en: I'll ask you to raise your hand, whether you are liberal, left of center --

cues.en: on social issues, primarily --

cues.zh: 还是保守派。
cues.en: or conservative.

cues.en: And I'll give a third option,

cues.en: because I know there are libertarians in the audience.

cues.en: So please raise your hand -- in the simulcast rooms too.

cues.en: Let's let everybody see who's here.

cues.en: Please raise your hand if you'd say that you're liberal or left of center.

cues.en: Please raise your hand high right now. OK.

cues.en: Please raise your hand if you'd say you're libertarian.

cues.en: OK. About two dozen.

cues.en: And please raise your hand if you'd say you are right of center or conservative.

cues.zh: 一、二、三、四、五——大约八到十个。
cues.en: One, two, three, four, five -- about eight or 10.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: OK.

cues.en: This is a bit of a problem.

cues.en: Because if our goal is to seek a deeper understanding of the world,

cues.zh: 我们这里普遍缺乏道德多样性，会让这件事更难。
cues.en: our general lack of moral diversity here is going to make it harder.

cues.zh: 因为当人们都共享价值观、都共享道德时，
cues.en: Because when people all share values, when people all share morals,

cues.zh: 他们就成了一支团队。
cues.en: they become a team.

cues.zh: 一旦引入团队心理，
cues.en: And once you engage the psychology of teams,

cues.zh: 它就会关闭开放性思维。
cues.en: it shuts down open-minded thinking.

cues.zh: 当自由派团队输了，
cues.en: When the liberal team loses,

cues.zh: 就像2004年那样，也像2000年几乎发生的那样，
cues.en: as it did in 2004, and as it almost did in 2000,

cues.zh: 我们会自我安慰。
cues.en: we comfort ourselves.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我们试图解释为什么一半的美国人投票给了另一支团队。
cues.en: We try to explain why half of America voted for the other team.

cues.zh: 我们认为他们一定是被宗教蒙蔽了，
cues.en: We think they must be blinded by religion

cues.zh: 或者只是单纯的愚蠢。
cues.en: or by simple stupidity.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: So if you think that half of America votes Republican

cues.zh: 是因为他们被这种方式蒙蔽了，
cues.en: because they are blinded in this way,

cues.zh: 那么我要告诉你的是，你被困在了一个道德矩阵中，
cues.en: then my message to you is that you're trapped in a moral Matrix,

cues.zh: 一个特定的道德矩阵。
cues.en: in a particular moral Matrix.

cues.zh: 我说的“矩阵”，就是字面意义上的矩阵，就像电影《黑客帝国》里的那样。
cues.en: And by "the Matrix," I mean literally the Matrix, like the movie "The Matrix."

cues.zh: 但我今天来这里是要给你一个选择。
cues.en: But I'm here today to give you a choice.

cues.zh: 你可以选择蓝色药丸，坚持你那些令人安慰的错觉，
cues.en: You can either take the blue pill and stick to your comforting delusions,

cues.zh: 或者你可以选择红色药丸，
cues.en: or you can take the red pill,

cues.zh: 学一点道德心理学，
cues.en: learn some moral psychology

cues.zh: 然后走出道德矩阵。
cues.en: and step outside the moral Matrix.

cues.zh: 现在，因为我知道——
cues.en: Now, because I know --

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: 我想这已经回答了我的问题。
cues.en: I assume that answers my question.

cues.zh: 我本来想问你们选了哪个，但没必要了。
cues.en: I was going to ask which one you picked, but no need.

cues.zh: 你们都对体验持高度开放的态度，
cues.en: You're all high in openness to experience,

cues.zh: 而且看起来它甚至可能味道不错，你们都是美食家。
cues.en: and it looks like it might even taste good, and you're all epicures.

cues.zh: 总之，我们就选红色药丸吧，研究一下道德心理学
cues.en: Anyway, let's go with the red pill, study some moral psychology

cues.zh: 看看它会带我们走向何方。
cues.en: and see where it takes us.

cues.zh: 让我们从头开始：什么是道德，它从何而来？
cues.en: Let's start at the beginning: What is morality, where does it come from?

cues.zh: 整个心理学中最糟糕的观点
cues.en: The worst idea in all of psychology

cues.zh: 就是认为人出生时心灵是一块白板。
cues.en: is the idea that the mind is a blank slate at birth.

cues.zh: 发展心理学已经表明，孩子们来到这个世界时
cues.en: Developmental psychology has shown that kids come into the world

cues.zh: 就已经对物理世界和社会世界了解了很多
cues.en: already knowing so much about the physical and social worlds

cues.zh: 并且天生就让他们很容易学会某些东西
cues.en: and programmed to make it really easy for them to learn certain things

cues.zh: 而很难学会另一些东西。
cues.en: and hard to learn others.

cues.zh: 我见过的最好的先天性的定义，
cues.en: The best definition of innateness I've seen,

cues.zh: 它为我澄清了很多事情，
cues.en: which clarifies so many things for me,

cues.zh: 来自脑科学家 Gary Marcus。
cues.en: is from the brain scientist Gary Marcus.

cues.zh: 他说：“大脑的初始结构
cues.en: He says, "The initial organization of the brain

cues.zh: 并不那么依赖于经验。
cues.en: does not depend that much on experience.

cues.zh: 天性提供了初稿，经验随后对其进行修订。
cues.en: Nature provides a first draft, which experience then revises.

cues.zh: ‘内置’并不意味着不可塑；
cues.en: 'Built-in' doesn't mean unmalleable;

cues.zh: 它意味着在经验之前就已组织好。”
cues.en: it means organized in advance of experience."

cues.zh: 那么，道德心智的初稿上有什么？
cues.en: OK, so what's on the first draft of the moral mind?

cues.zh: 为了找到答案，我和同事 Craig Joseph 通读了文献
cues.en: To find out, my colleague Craig Joseph and I read through the literature

cues.zh: 涉及人类学、道德的文化差异
cues.en: on anthropology, on culture variation in morality

cues.zh: 以及进化心理学，
cues.en: and also on evolutionary psychology,

cues.zh: 寻找匹配之处：
cues.en: looking for matches:

cues.zh: 在不同学科中，人们谈论的哪些东西
cues.en: What sorts of things do people talk about across disciplines

cues.zh: 是跨文化、甚至跨物种都能找到的？
cues.en: that you find across cultures and even species?

cues.zh: 我们找到了五个最佳匹配，称之为道德的五大基础。
cues.en: We found five best matches, which we call the five foundations of morality.

cues.zh: 第一个是伤害/关爱。
cues.en: The first one is harm/care.

cues.zh: 我们都是哺乳动物，都有大量神经和激素层面的编程
cues.en: We're all mammals here, we all have a lot of neural and hormonal programming

cues.zh: 让我们与他人紧密联结、关爱他人、
cues.en: that makes us really bond with others, care for others,

cues.zh: 对他人产生同情，尤其是对弱小和脆弱者。
cues.en: feel compassion for others, especially the weak and vulnerable.

cues.zh: 它让我们对那些造成伤害的人产生强烈的情绪。
cues.en: It gives us very strong feelings about those who cause harm.

cues.zh: 这个道德基础构成了我在TED听到的
cues.en: This moral foundation underlies about 70 percent

cues.zh: 大约70%的道德表述的根基。
cues.en: of the moral statements I've heard here at TED.

cues.zh: 第二个基础是公平/互惠。
cues.en: The second foundation is fairness/reciprocity.

cues.zh: 实际上，关于是否能在其他动物身上
cues.en: There's actually ambiguous evidence

cues.zh: 找到互惠行为，证据并不明确，
cues.en: as to whether you find reciprocity in other animals,

cues.zh: 但对于人类，证据再清楚不过了。
cues.en: but the evidence for people could not be clearer.

cues.zh: 这幅诺曼·洛克威尔的画作名为《黄金法则》——
cues.en: This Norman Rockwell painting is called "The Golden Rule" --

cues.zh: 正如卡伦·阿姆斯特朗所说，它是许多宗教的根基。
cues.en: as we heard from Karen Armstrong, it's the foundation of many religions.

cues.zh: 这第二个基础构成了我在TED听到的
cues.en: That second foundation underlies the other 30 percent

cues.zh: 另外30%的道德表述的根基。
cues.en: of the moral statements I've heard here at TED.

cues.zh: 第三个基础是内群体/忠诚。
cues.en: The third foundation is in-group/loyalty.

cues.zh: 在动物界确实存在合作群体，
cues.en: You do find cooperative groups in the animal kingdom,

cues.zh: 但这些群体要么非常小，要么全是兄弟姐妹。
cues.en: but these groups are always either very small or they're all siblings.

cues.zh: 只有在人类中，你才会发现非常大的群体
cues.en: It's only among humans that you find very large groups of people

cues.zh: 能够合作并联合成群体，
cues.en: who are able to cooperate and join together into groups,

cues.zh: 但在这里，群体是联合起来对抗其他群体的。
cues.en: but in this case, groups that are united to fight other groups.

cues.zh: 这很可能源于我们悠久的部落生活历史和部落心理。
cues.en: This probably comes from our long history of tribal living, of tribal psychology.

cues.zh: 而这种部落心理带来的愉悦如此深厚
cues.en: And this tribal psychology is so deeply pleasurable

cues.zh: 以至于即使我们没有部落，也会主动去组建，
cues.en: that even when we don't have tribes, we go ahead and make them,

cues.zh: 因为这很有趣。
cues.en: because it's fun.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 体育之于战争，正如色情之于性。
cues.en: Sports is to war as pornography is to sex.

cues.zh: 我们得以释放一些古老的驱动力。
cues.en: We get to exercise some ancient drives.

cues.zh: 第四个基础是权威/尊重。
cues.en: The fourth foundation is authority/respect.

cues.zh: 这里你看到的是顺从的姿态
cues.en: Here you see submissive gestures

cues.zh: 来自两个亲缘关系非常近的物种的成员。
cues.en: from two members of very closely related species.

cues.zh: 但人类的权威并不像其他灵长类动物那样
cues.en: But authority in humans is not so closely based on power and brutality

cues.zh: 那么基于权力和残暴。
cues.en: as it is in other primates.

cues.zh: 它更多基于自愿的顺从，有时甚至带有爱的成分。
cues.en: It's based on more voluntary deference and even elements of love, at times.

cues.zh: 第五个基础是纯洁/神圣。
cues.en: The fifth foundation is purity/sanctity.

cues.zh: 这幅画叫作《贞洁的寓言》，
cues.en: This painting is called "The Allegory Of Chastity,"

cues.zh: 但纯洁不仅仅是压制女性的性欲。
cues.en: but purity is not just about suppressing female sexuality.

cues.zh: 它关乎任何一种意识形态、任何一种观念，
cues.en: It's about any kind of ideology, any kind of idea

cues.zh: 告诉你只要控制自己的身体行为，
cues.en: that tells you that you can attain virtue by controlling what you do with your body

cues.zh: 控制你摄入身体的东西，就能获得美德。
cues.en: and what you put into your body.

cues.zh: 虽然政治右派更爱对性进行道德说教，
cues.en: And while the political right may moralize sex much more,

cues.zh: 政治左派则在食物上大做文章。
cues.en: the political left is doing a lot of it with food.

cues.zh: 如今食物正变得极度道德化。
cues.en: Food is becoming extremely moralized nowadays.

cues.zh: 很多是关于纯洁的观念，
cues.en: A lot of it is ideas about purity,

cues.zh: 关于你愿意触碰或吃进身体的东西。
cues.en: about what you're willing to touch or put into your body.

cues.zh: 我相信这五个是最佳候选，
cues.en: I believe these are the five best candidates

cues.zh: 对应道德大脑初稿上所写的内容。
cues.en: for what's written on the first draft of the moral mind.

cues.zh: 我认为这就是我们与生俱来的，一种学习所有这些事物的准备。
cues.en: I think this is what we come with, a preparedness to learn all these things.

cues.en: But as my son Max grows up in a liberal college town,

cues.en: how is this first draft going to get revised?

cues.en: And how will it end up being different

cues.en: from a kid born 60 miles south of us, in Lynchburg, Virginia?

cues.zh: 要思考文化的差异，让我们尝试一个不同的比喻。
cues.en: To think about culture variation, let's try a different metaphor.

cues.zh: 如果心智中确实有五个系统在运作，
cues.en: If there really are five systems at work in the mind,

cues.zh: 五个直觉和情感的来源，
cues.en: five sources of intuitions and emotions,

cues.zh: 那么我们可以把道德心智想象成那些音频均衡器之一
cues.en: then we can think of the moral mind as one of those audio equalizers

cues.zh: 它有五个频道，
cues.en: that has five channels,

cues.zh: 你可以为每个频道设置不同的设置。
cues.en: where you can set it to a different setting on every channel.

cues.zh: 我的同事Brian Nosek、Jesse Graham和我
cues.en: My colleagues Brian Nosek and Jesse Graham and I

cues.zh: 制作了一份问卷，我们把它放在了网上，网址是www.YourMorals.org。
cues.en: made a questionnaire, which we put up on the web at www.YourMorals.org.

cues.zh: 到目前为止，已有三万人填写了这份问卷，你也可以参与。
cues.en: And so far, 30,000 people have taken this questionnaire, and you can, too.

cues.zh: 这是大约两万三千名美国公民的调查结果。
cues.en: Here are the results from about 23,000 American citizens.

cues.zh: 左边是自由派的得分；
cues.en: On the left are the scores for liberals;

cues.zh: 你接受这一点吗？
cues.en: Do you accept this?

cues.zh: 你接受退出善恶之争吗？
cues.en: Do you accept stepping out of the battle of good and evil?

cues.zh: 你能做到不支持也不反对任何事吗？
cues.en: Can you be not for or against anything?

cues.zh: 那意义何在？你该怎么做？
cues.en: So what's the point? What should you do?

cues.zh: 如果你把最深刻的洞见
cues.en: Well, if you take the greatest insights

cues.zh: 从亚洲古代哲学和宗教中提炼出来
cues.en: from ancient Asian philosophies and religions

cues.zh: 再结合道德心理学的最新研究，
cues.en: and combine them with the latest research on moral psychology,

cues.zh: 我想你会得出这些结论：
cues.en: I think you come to these conclusions:

cues.zh: 我们那正义的大脑是进化设计出来的
cues.en: that our righteous minds were designed by evolution

cues.zh: 让我们团结成团队，
cues.en: to unite us into teams,

cues.zh: 让我们分裂、对抗其他团队
cues.en: to divide us against other teams

cues.zh: 然后让我们对真相视而不见。
cues.en: and then to blind us to the truth.

cues.zh: 那你该怎么做？
cues.en: So what should you do?

cues.zh: 我是在告诉你不去努力吗？
cues.en: Am I telling you to not strive?

cues.zh: 我是在告诉你去拥抱僧璨然后停下，
cues.en: Am I telling you to embrace Sēngcàn and stop,

cues.zh: 停下那支持与反对的挣扎吗？
cues.en: stop with the struggle of for and against?

cues.zh: 不，绝对不是。我不是那个意思。
cues.en: No, absolutely not. I'm not saying that.

cues.zh: 这是一群了不起的人，他们做了那么多事，
cues.en: This is an amazing group of people who are doing so much,

cues.zh: 付出了那么多才华、
cues.en: using so much of their talent,

cues.zh: 智慧、精力、金钱，
cues.en: their brilliance, their energy, their money,

cues.zh: 让世界变得更美好，
cues.en: to make the world a better place,

cues.zh: 去对抗不公，
cues.en: to fight wrongs,

cues.zh: 去解决问题。
cues.en: to solve problems.

cues.zh: 但正如我们从 Samantha Power 那里学到的，
cues.en: But as we learned from Samantha Power

cues.zh: 在她讲述 Sérgio Vieira de Mello 的故事中，
cues.en: in her story about Sérgio Vieira de Mello,

cues.zh: 你不能就这么冲进去说：“你错了，我对了，”
cues.en: you can't just go charging in, saying, "You're wrong, and I'm right,"

cues.zh: 因为，正如我们刚刚听到的，每个人都认为自己对。
cues.en: because, as we just heard, everybody thinks they are right.

cues.zh: 我们要解决的很多问题，
cues.en: A lot of the problems we have to solve

cues.zh: 都需要我们去改变别人。
cues.en: are problems that require us to change other people.

cues.zh: 而如果你想改变别人，
cues.en: And if you want to change other people,

cues.zh: 更好的办法是先理解我们是谁——
cues.en: a much better way to do it is to first understand who we are --

cues.zh: 理解我们的道德心理学，
cues.en: understand our moral psychology,

cues.zh: 理解我们都认为自己对——
cues.en: understand that we all think we're right --

cues.zh: 然后走出来，
cues.en: and then step out,

cues.zh: 哪怕只是一瞬间，走出来——去问问 Sēngcàn。
cues.en: even if it's just for a moment, step out -- check in with Sēngcàn.

cues.zh: 走出道德的矩阵，
cues.en: Step out of the moral Matrix,

cues.zh: 试着把它看作一场正在上演的较量，
cues.en: just try to see it as a struggle playing out,

cues.zh: 在其中每个人都认为自己是对的，即使你不同意他们，
cues.en: in which everybody thinks they're right, and even if you disagree with them,

cues.zh: 每个人做事都有自己的理由。
cues.en: everybody has some reasons for what they're doing.

cues.zh: 走出来。
cues.en: Step out.

cues.zh: 如果你这样做，这就是培养道德谦逊的关键一步，
cues.en: And if you do that, that's the essential move to cultivate moral humility,

cues.zh: 让自己摆脱这种自以为是，
cues.en: to get yourself out of this self-righteousness,

cues.zh: 而这正是人类的常态。
cues.en: which is the normal human condition.

cues.zh: 想想达赖喇嘛。
cues.en: Think about the Dalai Lama.

cues.zh: 想想达赖喇嘛那巨大的道德权威。
cues.en: Think about the enormous moral authority of the Dalai Lama.

cues.zh: 它来自他的道德谦逊。
cues.en: It comes from his moral humility.

cues.zh: 所以我认为重点——
cues.en: So I think the point --

cues.zh: 我演讲的重点，也是我认为TED的重点——
cues.en: the point of my talk and, I think, the point of TED --

cues.zh: 在于这是一个充满热情地投入
cues.en: is that this is a group that is passionately engaged

cues.zh: 追求让世界变得更好的群体。
cues.en: in the pursuit of changing the world for the better.

cues.zh: 这里的人们充满热情地投入
cues.en: People here are passionately engaged

cues.zh: 努力让世界变得更美好。
cues.en: in trying to make the world a better place.

cues.zh: 但同时也怀着对真理的热忱追求。
cues.en: But there is also a passionate commitment to the truth.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，答案就是利用这份对真理的热忱追求，
cues.en: And so I think the answer is to use that passionate commitment to the truth

cues.zh: 努力把它转化为我们所有人更美好的未来。
cues.en: to try to turn it into a better future for us all.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
